chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated: `Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'dabadi, from Ahmad ibn Abu `Abd Allah al-Barqi, from his father, from Rabi' al-Warraq, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu `Abd Allah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'Every thing is perishable but His Face.' He (AS) said: 'We.'

key_terms.وَجْهَهُ: His Face (metaphor for essence or the Imams)

ai.seo_question: Who does 'His Face' refer to in the verse 'Every thing is perishable but His Face'?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets 'His Face' (Wajh) in Surah Al-Qasas as referring to the Imams, grounding the concept of divine permanence in their spiritual reality. This interpretation aligns with the Shia doctrine of *Tawassul* and the eternal nature of the Imamate, distinguishing the infallible guides from the transient creation. It underscores the Imams' role as the ultimate locus of divine worship and the means through which believers connect to Allah.
